expected_level_description: You can: - manage a ledger or transaction process and keep it accurate and up to date - investigate and clear complex reconciling items and aged balances - improve transaction processes, for example by automating matching or approvals - train and check the work of other staff

You can: - prepare month-end and year-end entries, such as accruals, prepayments, and provisions - prepare sections of the annual accounts and supporting notes - apply accounting standards to routine transactions, such as capitalising software and hardware

You can: - prepare monthly budget reports and explain the main variances - code costs correctly between cost centres, projects, and capital and revenue - support budget holders to understand and manage their budgets

You can: - administer the finance or payroll system, including access, workflows, and reporting - design reports and dashboards for budget holders - test system changes and upgrades - automate repetitive finance tasks

You can: - test and improve the controls for a financial process - manage audit requests for an area and agree actions on findings - write and update financial procedures - work with counter-fraud specialists to reduce fraud risk
You can: - prepare tax returns and reconciliations under supervision - apply the right tax treatment to common purchases and income - check employment status for contractors under guidance

You can: - apply the organisation's capital and revenue rules to everyday spending - explain how funding allocations and spending limits affect your area - recognise spending that needs approval from a funder or spending control

You can: - identify important stakeholders and communicate with them clearly and regularly - tailor communication to stakeholders' needs and work with them to build relationships while meeting user needs - build and reach consensus with stakeholders - work to improve stakeholder relationships using evidence to explain decisions
You can: - supervise day-to-day work and give feedback - take part in recruitment and induction - hold regular one-to-one conversations
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
